角笛為文藝復興時期的雙簧樂器，現有證據僅來自 Michael Praetoriu: The cornamuse is a Renaissance double-reed instrument, and the only evidence for it is Michael Praetorius's Syntagma musicum II, published in 1619; as no instrument or picture of the period survives, later reconstructions all contain conjecture. Praetorius describes it as similar to the crumhorn, with the reed inside a wind cap and a cylindrical body, but unlike double-bore instruments such as the sordun, kortholt and curtal it has a single bore, and it is close to the schryari in size and appearance. Its name must not be confused with the French word for bagpipe.
角笛的聆聽示範主要見於文藝復興時期歐洲古樂的重建演奏場合。由於現存無當時實物或圖: Listening examples of the cornamuse come mainly from reconstructions of Renaissance European early music. Since no instrument or picture of the period survives, what is heard generally comes from rebuilt instruments made on the description in book two of Michael Praetorius's Syntagma musicum. The source mentions no particular pieces or line-up, so a demonstration usually presents a single instrument, or compares it with a close relative such as the crumhorn, to show its smaller volume and its soft timbre close to the crumhorn's.
角笛（Cornamuse）是文藝復興時期歐洲的雙簧樂器，H-S編號422.111: The cornamuse is a Renaissance European double-reed instrument, H-S number 422.111. It is built like the crumhorn, with the reed inside a wind cap, a cylindrical body and a single bore; the bottom is closed and small side holes let out the resonance. It is known only from Praetorius's written description, and no instrument or picture of the period has been found; there is no clear record of how or by whom it was used, and later reconstructions are mostly conjecture.
